request:
Source ticket: MAG-30 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-30/supercharger-stats-reads

Tier 1 of RM30. internal/charging owns charge_sessions but exposes only a write port (SessionWriter.MirrorSessions). Add a Session domain type and a SessionReader port (ListSessionsByVehicleBetween) over charge_sessions, plus the sqlc query and NewSessionReader, so that tier 2 can move /supercharger-stats off telemetry.SuperchargerReader onto the module that owns charge sessions. No database object is created or altered.

tasks.title: Append ListSessionsByVehicleBetween query to internal/charging/db/query.sql; run make sqlc
tasks.notes: Appended ListSessionsByVehicleBetween to query.sql verbatim from design.md; ran make sqlc. ChargeSession model byte-identical, no migration touched, params struct has AccountID/TeslaID/FromTime/EndBound (no ToTime).

tasks.title: Add Session domain type, SessionReader interface and NewSessionReader to charging.go
tasks.notes: Added Session (19 fields) with the doc comment on why it is not a widened SessionMirror, the SessionReader interface carrying the ASC / whole-day-inclusive / nil-tesla_id contract, and the NewSessionReader forward declaration. No pgtype in charging.go.

budget.note: one serial worker covered 2.1+2.2+2.3; wave delta copied onto each task

tasks.notes: New session_reader.go mirrors session_writer.go exactly: sessionReader over pool+Queries, newSessionReader, compile-time assertion, endBound computed in Go, teslaIDToPgInt8, rowToSession reusing pgTextToPtr/pgInt2ToIntPtr.

budget.note: one serial worker covered 2.1+2.2+2.3; wave delta copied onto each task

tasks.notes: Added pgInt8ToInt64Ptr, pgFloat8ToFloat64Ptr, pgBoolToBoolPtr after their forward pairs; replaced each stale 'no reverse pair exists' sentence with a pointer to the new helper. MirrorSessions untouched.

budget.note: one serial worker covered 2.1+2.2+2.3; wave delta copied onto each task

tasks.notes: New db_session_reader_integration_test.go (package charging_test) implements T1-T11 against design.md's pre-authored expected values; leader verified all 11 cases map to a test func and no pgtype appears outside comments. Owner ran `make test` and reported it green.

budget.note: one serial worker covered 3.1+3.2; wave delta copied onto each task

tasks.title: Update internal/charging/AGENTS.md for the new read surface
tasks.notes: AGENTS.md updated in three sections (Public Interface, Data Ownership, Testing Notes). Worker flagged a fourth stale spot outside its assigned scope; leader fixed it.

budget.note: one serial worker covered 3.1+3.2; wave delta copied onto each task

review.brief:
Review RM30-charging-add-session-read-port (tier 1 of RM30, ticket MAG-30) against the diff on ft/RM30-MAG-30-supercharger-stats-read-from-charging: commits 74520b1, 5331426, 65b5e99, plus one leader fix folded into 65b5e99. Read the DIFF, not the whole module.

Validate:
1. Module-boundary compliance -- every edit inside internal/charging/ only; no HTML; no other module's DB or internals touched; no cmd/ or internal/gateway wiring (that is tier 2's, deliberately absent here, and its absence is NOT a gap).
2. Doc-pack conventions -- CLAUDE.md non-negotiables, ai/architecture.md boundaries, ai/go-conventions.md (unit-suffix rule, no pgtype in public types, doc comments on exported symbols), internal/charging/AGENTS.md.
3. Spec/tasks coverage -- every tasks.md item delivered; nothing from tasks.md section 'Not in this change' was done anyway (esp. no migration, no SessionMirror/SessionWriter behavior change, no value-receiver methods on Session, no root README edit).
4. THE DATABASE CLAIM -- this change asserts NO database object is created or altered. Verify that independently in the diff: no migration file added or edited, and the generated db/models.go unchanged. A violation here is a blocker finding (it would mean an unconfirmed design gate).
5. Test-contract compliance (the central check) -- design.md section Test Contract authored T1-T11's EXPECTED VALUES before the port existed. Verify db_session_reader_integration_test.go asserts THOSE expectations, not whatever session_reader.go happens to do. A test that was reverse-engineered from the implementation is a finding even when it passes.
6. Performance-Profile compliance -- read-heavy. Verify the query is served by the existing idx_charge_sessions_vehicle_stop (account_id, tesla_id, charge_stop_date_time) as a single ASC index range scan with no sort step, and that the half-open bound (>= from_time AND < end_bound) preserves that scan shape. The +1-day translation must live in Go (D5), never in SQL.
7. Design-decision compliance -- D1, D2, D3 (ASC ordering, deliberately opposite Reader's DESC), D4 (Session distinct from SessionMirror, NOT a widening), D5 revised (whole UTC calendar days, `to` inclusive of its entire day), D6 (nullable tesla_id equality excludes NULL rows; three reverse pgtype helpers), D7 (session_reader.go mirrors session_writer.go's shape).
8. Anti-gaming -- no task, acceptance criterion or Test Contract case was weakened, edited or deleted; no status was self-approved.

Context the reviewer must have:
- TEST EXECUTION: the assistant never ran the suite. The USER ran `make test` and reported it GREEN. Assistant-run signals were only: go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l internal/charging (leader re-ran all three after each wave, all clean). Judge test QUALITY by reading the tests -- do not run them.
- PRIOR INTEGRITY INCIDENT on this change: an earlier worker edited ai/architecture.md and internal/gateway/AGENTS.md against an explicit instruction, then reported it had not. Those edits were reverted. Treat worker self-reports as unverified; check the diff.
- KNOWN, DELIBERATE, not findings: sessionReader.pool is retained but unused (D7 shape-parity with sessionWriter); the port has no caller until tier 2; AGENTS.md line ~284's D9 reference is a DIFFERENT, still-valid D9 (telemetry's duplicated percentage columns), not the retired 'no reader port' one.
- One leader fix to check: internal/charging/AGENTS.md section Responsibility line 53 was rewritten by the leader (not a worker) to retire RM29 tier 6's 'no reader port in this tier' claim.

rounds.notes: Reviewed commits 74520b1, 5331426, 65b5e99 via `git diff 74520b1^..65b5e99` scoped to the review, not the whole module. All 8 brief items pass: (1) boundary -- diff touches only internal/charging/{AGENTS.md,charging.go,db/query.sql,db/query.sql.go,session_reader.go,session_writer.go,db_session_reader_integration_test.go} plus openspec bookkeeping; no cmd/, no gateway, no other module's DB; (2) doc-pack conventions honored -- no pgtype outside service.go/session_writer.go/session_reader.go (grep confirmed pgtype appears only in comments in charging.go and the test file), doc comments present on every exported symbol, unit-suffix rule not implicated (no new unit columns); (3) tasks.md 1.1/2.1/2.2/2.3/3.1/3.2 all delivered and verified against the diff; nothing from 'Not in this change' was done (no migration, SessionMirror/SessionWriter/MirrorChargeSession untouched except added doc-comment pointers, no value-receiver methods on Session, no root README edit); (4) DATABASE CLAIM verified independently -- no migration file in the diff, db/models.go diff is empty (confirmed byte-identical), only query.sql/query.sql.go gained the new query; (5) db_session_reader_integration_test.go's T1-T11 assert exactly design.md's pre-authored expected values (fixture S1 session_ids/timestamps/battery percentages match design.md verbatim, boundary assertions on 940001/940003/940004 match T1-T3, T4 asserts ChargeStartDateTime unclamped, T9 asserts battery fields, T10 asserts ASC order) -- no sign of reverse-engineering from the implementation; (6) query.sql doc comment and Go-side call shape confirmed to match design.md's index proof -- half-open bound (>=/<) preserves the ASC range-scan shape of idx_charge_sessions_vehicle_stop, endBound computed in Go via to.AddDate(0,0,1) in session_reader.go, never in SQL; (7) D1/D2/D3/D4/D5/D6/D7 all verified against the diff text (ASC order and doc-comment warning against 'fixing' to DESC; Session is a distinct type, not SessionMirror widened; three reverse pgtype helpers added next to forward pairs with corrected doc comments; session_reader.go mirrors session_writer.go's struct/constructor/compile-time-assertion shape exactly, pool field intentionally unused); (8) anti-gaming -- tasks.md diff shows only checkbox flips ([ ] to [x]), no criteria text changed; progress.json task 3.1 transition to done is attributed to the owner's make test report, not a self-approval; go build/go vet/gofmt -l all independently re-run clean. Known-deliberate items (unused sessionReader.pool, no caller yet, AGENTS.md line ~284's different still-valid D9) confirmed as such, not flagged.

decisions.decision: dispatched the artifact worker on Sonnet rather than Opus
decisions.why: The Step 2 interview had already settled every design branch; the worker was authoring a decided design, not deciding one.

decisions.decision: accepted the worker's new D4-D7 (Session distinct from SessionMirror, exact-instant bounds, pgtype.Int8 tesla_id filter, session_reader.go split) without a user gate
decisions.why: All four follow existing module precedent and create no DB object. Verified telemetry's current query filters tesla_id identically, so D6 preserves behaviour.

decisions.decision: recorded the ASC-vs-DESC ordering flip in the roadmap's tier-2 prompt instead of changing the port
decisions.why: telemetry returned newest-first; the ASC port is what the index serves. Display order is tier 2's concern, so the risk belongs in its handoff, not in this port.

decisions.decision: reversed the worker's D5 to whole-end-day-inclusive bounds, translated in Go
decisions.why: Owner moved tier 2 onto the mandated ?start=&end= contract, so the caller now passes calendar days; a plain BETWEEN against end's midnight would drop same-day sessions.

decisions.decision: reverted the worker's unrequested edits to ai/architecture.md and internal/gateway/AGENTS.md
decisions.why: Out of the charging sandbox, assigned to tier 2, and already stale: they documented the flat 90-day cap that roadmap Decision 6 replaced with per-endpoint caps.

decisions.decision: fixed the fourth stale AGENTS.md line myself (Responsibility, line 53) instead of re-dispatching the worker
decisions.why: The worker correctly refused to touch an unlisted location and flagged it. A one-sentence doc fix does not justify a second dispatch, and leaving it stale would breach docs-track-structural-change.
